episodes.title: Intro to History of Science
episodes.description: Introduce the long history of people investigating fundamental questions about the natural world.

episodes.title: The Presocratics
episodes.description: Meet the Presocratic philosophers and their attempts to distinguish natural knowledge from myth.

episodes.title: Plato and Aristotle
episodes.description: Explore Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle and their contributions to ancient philosophy and the study of nature.

episodes.title: India
episodes.description: Today, Hank takes us to India to talk Vedas, Maurya Empires, and some really good doctoring.

episodes.title: The Americas and Time Keeping
episodes.description: Explore how Maya, Inca, and Olmec civilizations recorded knowledge and kept track of time.

episodes.title: Roman Engineering
episodes.description: Examine Roman engineering through the distinction between practical craft and theoretical knowledge.

episodes.title: The Medieval Islamicate World
episodes.description: The religion of Islam significantly influenced knowledge-making in the greater Mediterranean and western Asian world.

episodes.title: Medieval China
episodes.description: Today, we’re going to focus on the time of the Northern and Southern Song Dynasties, a time of great technical innovation.

episodes.title: Ancient & Medieval Medicine
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course History of Science, Hank Green explains how medicine has progressed over time.

episodes.title: Alchemy
episodes.description: Explore how alchemists combined experiments and theories of matter to develop knowledge about the natural world.

episodes.title: Cathedrals and Universities
episodes.description: Trace the roles of monasteries, Gothic cathedrals, and emerging universities in medieval knowledge-making.

episodes.title: The Scientific Revolution
episodes.description: Investigate what historians mean by a scientific revolution.

episodes.title: The New Astronomy
episodes.description: Explore how observations that challenged existing astronomy contributed to the Scientific Revolution.

episodes.title: The Scientific Methods
episodes.description: Examine the historical diversity of methods scientists have used to investigate nature.

episodes.title: The New Anatomy
episodes.description: Explore books, experiments, and microscopy as tools for investigating anatomy and the nature of life.

episodes.title: The Columbian Exchange
episodes.description: Explore how the Age of Exploration shaped scientific knowledge-making between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries.

episodes.title: Newton and Leibniz
episodes.description: Explore Newton and Leibniz’s place in the Scientific Revolution and the development of physics.

episodes.title: The New Chemistry
episodes.description: Examine how chemistry’s development complicates the idea of a single Scientific Revolution.

episodes.title: Biology Before Darwin
episodes.description: Examine how seventeenth- and eighteenth-century thinkers understood life before Darwin’s work.

episodes.title: Earth Science
episodes.description: Explore the origins of geology and the questions fossils raised about Earth’s past.

episodes.title: The Industrial Revolution
episodes.description: Explore nineteenth-century industrialization, from railways and urban growth to environmental destruction and divisions between social classes.

episodes.title: Darwin and Natural Selection
episodes.description: Darwin and Wallace are at the heart of understanding evolution and natural selection.

episodes.title: Eugenics and Francis Galton
episodes.description: Francis Galton and a few others decided natural selection could be used to make the human race "better" and came up with Eugenics.

episodes.title: Micro-Biology
episodes.description: Explore the historical development of knowledge about microscopic life.

episodes.title: Genetics – Lost and Found
episodes.description: This is the story of Gregor Mendel and how his work was done, lost, then found again.

episodes.title: Thermodynamics
episodes.description: It's time for Hank to talk about the history of Thermodynamics!!!

episodes.title: Electricity
episodes.description: Trace the study of electricity from antiquity through figures such as Galvani and Edison.

episodes.title: Ford, Cars, and a New Revolution
episodes.description: Explore debates about industrial change through the history of cars, manufacturing, and Henry Ford.

episodes.title: Cinema, Radio, and Television
episodes.description: Explore the origins of cinema, radio, and television and their roles in news, entertainment, and education.

episodes.title: The Mind/Brain
episodes.description: Explore how biological theories, experiments, and therapies shaped the emergence of modern brain sciences.

episodes.title: Marie Curie and Spooky Rays
episodes.description: Explore Marie Curie’s education and scientific discoveries despite the barriers she faced.

episodes.title: Einstein’s Revolution
episodes.description: Examine physics before Einstein and the changes associated with his work.

episodes.title: The Atomic Bomb
episodes.description: Trace the development of the atomic bomb, beginning with Einstein’s warning about the possibility of a German nuclear weapon.

episodes.title: Biomedicine
episodes.description: Trace advances in medicine grounded in biological explanations of the body and disease.

episodes.title: Genetics and The Modern Synthesis
episodes.description: Explore how biologists brought Darwin’s account of evolution and Mendelian inheritance together in the modern synthesis.

episodes.title: The Computer and Turing
episodes.description: Explore how World War II accelerated changes in computing.

episodes.title: Air Travel and The Space Race
episodes.description: Explore the postwar competition between the United States and Soviet Union to send satellites, animals, and people into space.

episodes.title: Ecology
episodes.description: Explore how ecology brought together ideas from biology and the earth sciences.

episodes.title: Controlling the Environment
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course History of Science, Hank Green teaches you about the pros and cons of humans controlling the environment.

episodes.title: Biotechnology
episodes.description: The history of discovering what DNA is, what it looks like, and how it works is... complicated.

episodes.title: Bodies and Dollars
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course History of Science, Hank Green takes a look at the rise of Big Pharma and GMO foods.

episodes.title: The Century of the Gene
episodes.description: Examine the limits of molecular explanations of life and the complexity that remains beyond identifying genes.

episodes.title: The Internet and Computing
episodes.description: Trace the development of computing and the internet, including possible futures and their connections to biotechnology.

episodes.title: Life and Longevity
episodes.description: Examine CRISPR, technologies that might extend life, and ethical questions surrounding human longevity.

episodes.title: Climate Science
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course History of Science, Hank talks to us about where climate science started and how it works today.

episodes.title: The Limits of History
episodes.description: Revisit people omitted from the series and consider why diversity matters in the history of science.
